maya: Quick heads-up — I spun up a staging bring-up for Lattice-embed v1.3b through the ONNX/int8 pipeline. Initial semantic tests show a recall@10 drop of ~3.2% vs prod (Falcon-emb-2) on the wiki holdout. Logging quick outputs below and asking for quick ideas on what to triage. :thinking_face:

kevin: Can you paste the eval command and the holdout slice you used? Also which index config (HNSW params) and normalization were applied?

maya: Eval command & sample results:
```
./eval_vectors --model lattice-1.3b-int8.onnx --dataset wiki-holdout-10k --metric recall@10 --norm l2 --index hnsw --ef_search 64 --ef_construction 200
results: recall@1=0.412, recall@5=0.642, recall@10=0.716 (prod: r@10=0.748)
silhouette=0.28, avg_cos_sim_top1=0.62
```

sophie: Noted. Did you apply post-whitening / mean-centering? Small shifts there can move recall a few points. Also check per-lang slices if this is multilingual noise.

maya: No whitening. I ran raw L2-normalize only. Per-lang looked similar but en had slightly bigger drop.

raj: @maya quick triage checklist: 1) rerun with whitening + length-scaled norm 2) compare cosine vs dot scoring (embedding scale differences after quant) 3) check KNN index seed/ef variability 4) run small KDE of distance distribution to look for mode shifts (centroid drift).

maya: Running whitening and cosine compare now — will post numbers. Also kicking off an index rebuild with ef_construction=400 to rule out index construction artifacts.

ci-bot: build/emb-eval #482 queued by maya — tests: basic-recall, silhouette, kmeans-5-purity. ETA ~12m. :gear:

kevin: If whitening recovers >1.5% r@10, that's a strong signal it's a post-processing mismatch. If not, try a float32 ONNX run to see quantization impact specifically (int8 dropout).

maya: Quick follow-up (prelim): whitening + cosine -> r@10=0.735 (delta +1.9%). float32 ONNX run queued; will compare int8 vs float32 to isolate quantization.

raj: Good. Also capture embedding norms pre/post-whitening and histograms. If norms compress under int8, quantization could squash fine-grained distinctions.

maya: Will attach histograms to PR once float32 job completes. Folks, any other quick requests before I start deeper root-cause?

sophie: Add a tiny synthetic probe: a set of near-duplicate pairs (known positives) and hard negatives — see if pairwise cosine gap narrows under int8. That pinpoints pair-level degradation.

maya: Added synthetic probe to CI pipeline. Thanks — I'll report back with the float32 vs int8 diff + KDE plots. :sparkles:
